# Spider silk sensing, encoded for transfer

Function: tell a trapped insect from the wind by touch alone. Behavior: a thin thread carries a vibration to the spider's legs, and the spider reads the rhythm of the shake to tell prey from a falling leaf. Structure: a tight radial web of silk anchored at a few points, with the spider resting on a signal line at the hub.

The point of keeping this encoding is the shape of the idea, not the spider: a thin line can be read by the pattern of its own vibration, without seeing it.
